title: Didn’t keep suction, or was it me?
text:
Didn’t keep suction, or was it me?. I’m trying to down size and move into Our beach home that is small, and I thought this is exactly what I need.
This comes with some type of pump to take the air out, which I did not use. I use a Panasonic vacuum that has allot of suction.
I folded a king size heavy blanket to give this a try. The bag is big, and the blanket did not fill the bag.
As I was closing the bag the zip up thing came off! But got it back on track. Took the cap off, and the vacuum suction the bag down. Did a good job.
But after a few minutes very slowly it was not suctioned tight!
I checked the bag to make sure it was sealed good , and kept using the vacuum to reseal it.
This would not keep suctioned down!
Don’t know if it’s a bad bag , or me, or my husband but this bag kept loosing suction

I’m really disappointed .

description: Easy to Use: 4 Simple Steps to Save Space and Keep Your Closet Organized!

Ensure that everything you want to store is clean and completely dry. Open up the bag on a flat surface and undo the zip. Fold the materials and put them inside the bag carefully. Stack items on top of each other, but do not overfill. Make sure that there are a couple of centimeters spare from the edges of the clothes etc and the zip closure.

With the items in place, use the plastic clip to zip along sealing the two plastic zips. Go back over the zips to ensure it is fully sealed. The surest way is to run the clip fully from end to end in both directions, and then to run your hand along the whole length of the zip between finger and thumb to ensure that there’s no tiny section missed. Please be noted that the clip is not fixed by design, so don’t panic when it falls off.

When ready, undo the valve lid by unscrewing it, and then place the vacuum cleaner nozzle with no attachments on it over the valve. You simply need to press it against the valve, and then turn the vacuum on. It will then start to remove the air. After vacuuming all the air out of the bag, stop and close the cap quickly to secure an air-tight seal. Listen carefully for any signs of air leaking out of the cap or other zipped parts of the bag. Repeat step 2 if necessary. If the bags are tightly sealed, congratulations, you can put them under your bed or wherever you think is suitable.
